battle.name: 陳平始興王陳叔陵叛亂
battle.brief: 開皇二年（582）正月，陳宣帝崩次日，湘東王陳叔陵在建康宮中舉兵，藥刀刺兄不中，敗走東府集甲士應援。陳後主遣蕭摩訶討之，蕭摩訶先誘捕其心腹戴溫、譚騏驎，再追截百餘步騎於南門。卡面的秦弩正是蕭摩訶賴以成名的步弩：既是他平叛的依托，也是他降隋後成為隋軍攻陳主力的那門技術。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這是一場發生在南朝陳朝京師建康的宮廷兵變，交戰雙方都不是國家，而是陳朝統治集團內部的兩股武裝力量。平叛一方是剛即位的陳後主陳叔寶與以尚書台為核心的朝廷：兵員來自京師宿衛、殿中侍衛與左右衛將軍所部，統兵主將是南陳最負盛名的弩將蕭摩訶，此人一生以步弩射術立身，宿衛出入與宮禁門禁的調度都在他手上。叛亂一方是宣帝次子、始興王陳叔陵；他出繼祖父陳道譚而得王封，十六歲便開府都督江郢晉三州諸軍事，後來歷任湘州刺史、揚州刺史、中軍大將軍、侍中，手裡握著州鎮的常備兵與自己的私人部曲，事發當夜在東府（揚州刺史治所）聚集甲士，散金銀為賞，企圖向外郡的諸王幕府與將帥發出號令，真正應命的只有堂弟、新安王陳伯固一人。叛軍並不打算固守建康，而是準備由南門突圍、投奔北方的隋朝，因為同年十月隋文帝已分道東下伐陳。宮廷之外還有北周降將與北方來使往來，宗室人人自危，這是陳叔陵鋌而走險的外部背景。
countriesEn: This was a palace rising fought in the Southern Chen capital of Jiankang; neither side was a state, but two armed factions inside the Chen ruling group. The side of the suppression was the newly enthroned Emperor Hou of Chen, Chen Shubao, and the court centred on the Department of State Affairs: the troops came from the capital garrison, the Palace Guard and the divisions of the Left and Right Guard Generals, and the field commander was Xiao Mohe, the most famous crossbowman of Southern Chen, a man whose whole reputation rested on the handheld crossbow and who held authority over the palace guard and the gates of the inner city. The rebel side was Chen Shuling, second son of Emperor Xuan of Chen and Prince of Shixing, who had inherited the title of his grandfather Chen Daotan; at sixteen he was already commanding the armies of Jiang, Ying and Jin as an accredited commander, and afterwards served as Governor of Xiang, Governor of Yangzhou, General of the Central Army and Attendant of the Imperial Residence, holding the standing garrisons of the provinces and his own private retainers. On the night of the rising he mustered armoured men at the Eastern Office, the seat of the Yangzhou Governor, scattered gold and silver as bounty, and tried to issue orders to the princely commanderies and generals abroad; the only man who answered was his cousin Chen Bogu, Prince of Xin'an. The rebels never meant to hold Jiankang: they planned to break out through the South Gate and run to the northern state of Sui, because in the same year the Sui emperor had already sent several armies east against Chen. Beyond the palace walls there were also former Northern Zhou officers and envoys from the north moving in and out of the capital, so that every member of the imperial clan felt himself surrounded, and this was the external background that pushed Chen Shuling into open rebellion.
people: 陳叔陵（554至582年）是這場叛亂的發動者，字子嵩，母彭氏，出繼祖父陳道譚，早年與兄長陳叔寶一同在建康作人質，歸陳之後封康樂侯，邑五百戶，十六歲封始興郡王並開府掌三州軍務。他性情嚴刻，屬下懼怕，多次調任江州、湘州、揚州，握有兵柄；太建十一年母喪丁憂，服闋復任侍中、中軍大將軍。宣帝病重時他已與心腹密議，宣帝正月甲寅崩，翌日即以淬了藥的刀砍傷兄長陳叔寶的頸項，意在奪位；叔寶的生母柳氏與乳母吳氏上前拉扯，長沙王陳叔堅與他角力奪下刀，用衣袖反縛於柱上，他掙脫後自雲龍門奔回東府，召甲士、散金銀為賞。新安王陳伯固是唯一響應的宗室，隨後被誅；叔陵的舅父彭暠及附逆官員亦被處決。蕭摩訶是平叛的主將，他沒有急攻，而是先詐稱必須由始興王的心腹大將親自出面才肯聽命，隨後捕獲親信戴溫、譚騏驎，送臺省斬首，懸於東城示眾；待叔陵自率步騎百餘人由南門突圍欲奔隋時，蕭摩訶率軍追截，叔陵落馬被斬。
peopleEn: Chen Shuling (554 to 582) was the man who set the rising in motion. His courtesy name was Zisong, his mother was of the Peng clan, and he had been adopted to continue the line of his grandfather Chen Daotan. As a boy he was held in Jiankang as a hostage together with his elder brother Chen Shubao, and after the family returned to Chen he was made Prince of Kangle with five hundred households of fief. At sixteen he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing and given an independent command over the armies of three provinces. His manner was harsh and exacting, his subordinates feared him, and he was moved repeatedly between Jiangzhou, Xiangzhou and Yangzhou, always holding troops in his own hand. In the eleventh year of Taijian his mother died and he went into mourning; when his period of retirement ended he was restored as Attendant and General of the Central Army. While Emperor Xuan lay dying he had already been conferring with his close followers. The emperor died on the jia-yin day of the first month, and the next day Chen Shuling struck at his brother Chen Shubao's neck with a blade steeped in poison, meaning to seize the throne by killing him outright; the emperor's mother, of the Liu clan, and the wet nurse Wu rushed at him, and the Prince of Changsha, Chen Shujian, grappled with him, wrenched the knife away and bound his arms with a sleeve to a column. Shuling tore himself loose, ran out through the Yunlong Gate and back to the Eastern Office, called in the armoured men and scattered gold and silver as bounty. Chen Bogu, Prince of Xin'an, was the only member of the imperial clan who answered the call, and he was executed; so was Chen Shuling's uncle Peng Gao and the officials who had joined the plot. Xiao Mohe commanded the suppression. He did not strike at once: he pretended that he would only listen if the Prince of Shixing's own trusted general came to him in person, and when the prince sent his intimates Dai Wen and Tan Qilin he seized them, sent them to the Department of State Affairs to be beheaded, and hung their heads at the East City to show the rebels what was coming. Only when Chen Shuling tried to break out with a hundred cavalry and foot soldiers through the South Gate in order to reach Sui did Xiao Mohe pursue and cut him down, after the prince fell from his horse.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩在這場衝突裡並不是什麼稀罕物，而是一個王朝的標準配備。弩的機關把拉力存住，射手不必像拉弓那樣先扯開弓弦再撒手，瞄準靠望山、擊發靠機牙，因此射速遠勝弓手，也更適合在狹窄的門道、宮道與城樓上做精確射擊；南陳的州鎮兵與京師宿衛裡，弩手往往單獨編制，不併入刀盾、長槍的步兵序列。蕭摩訶正是以步弩聞名：據《陳書》，太建四年北齊水軍進逼采石、造具裝船打算截斷航道時，他以弩射中齊軍舟船，迫其退卻；那種可以夾在臂下隨身攜帶的小弩，射速與精度都在弓之上。叛亂之夜真正動手的兵器卻不是弩：陳叔陵用的是一把淬了藥的刀，靠的是近身纏鬥，陳叔堅奪刀時用的是臂力；蕭摩訶用來誘敵的鼓吹儀仗，是南陳大將的法定排場，韋諒代叔陵把整副鼓吹送去蕭摩訶處，等於把自己的虛實與心腹名單一併送上門。守城一方沿用歷代的做法：把弩手佈在城樓與門道，把進攻者壓在牆外不許貼身；這一條在沒有大型攻城器械可用、只能靠巷戰與突門的宮廷兵變裡，同樣決定了誰能先站住位置。
kitsEn: The crossbow on the card face was nothing exotic in this clash; it was standard equipment for the dynasty. The lock mechanism stores the pull of the bow, so the shooter does not have to draw the string and then loose it as an archer must; the aim is taken with the sight and the shot is released by the trigger, which makes the rate of fire far better than that of a bow and makes the weapon well suited to precise shooting in narrow doorways, palace corridors and on the wall towers. In the provincial garrisons and the capital guard of Southern Chen, crossbowmen were usually mustered as a separate body and not absorbed into the sword-and-shield or long-spear infantry. Xiao Mohe was exactly the sort of man famous for the handheld crossbow: according to the Book of Chen, when the Northern Qi fleet pressed up to Caishi in the fourth year of Taijian and built armoured ships to cut the channel, he shot a bolt into one of the Qi vessels and drove it off; such a small crossbow carried under the arm has both a better rate of fire and better precision than a bow. The weapon that actually did the work on the night of the rising was not a crossbow: Chen Shuling used a blade steeped in poison and relied on close grappling, and it was raw strength that won the knife away when Chen Shujian closed with him. The drums and banners Xiao Mohe used to draw the rebels in were the ceremonial appurtenances of a general of Southern Chen; Wei Liang carried the whole set over to Xiao Mohe on Shuling's behalf, handing over his own situation and the list of his trusted men along with it. The defending side followed the practice of every earlier age: crossbowmen were posted on the towers and in the gateways to pin the attackers against the wall and stop them closing. In a palace rising where no heavy siege engines were available and everything had to be decided by street fighting and sudden attacks on the gates, that same rule decided who could seize a position first.
tactics: 整場兵變壓縮在皇城與外郭之間的幾里路內，全程不過一日。陳叔陵的部署是宮廷式奪位：先在宣帝病重時收攏心腹與金銀，再於宣帝崩後在雲龍門內動手，用藥刀解決兄長本人，再脫身回東府，以揚州刺史的權柄召集甲士、散財結士，企圖讓在外諸王將帥以為新君已被控制，最後把人馬集結起來由南門突出、奔隋求援。蕭摩訶的應手分三段：其一，不接受任何以三公宰輔為條件的勸降，反而提出須心腹大將親自前來的反條件，誘使對方把戴溫、譚騏驎送進自己的營中，擒斬後在東城示眾，先在士氣上把叛軍壓住；其二，率軍封住宮門與通往南門的通道，宿衛在門道兩側以弩待敵，弓弩的射界覆蓋街口，使叛軍無法展開；其三，待叔陵率步騎百餘人突圍時，集中兵馬在要道截擊，叔陵急於奔隋、落馬被斬，隨行步騎潰散。從兵種上看，這是一場典型的近距反叛：進攻方靠突門、亂戰與突圍，防守方靠門禁、封堵與定點射擊，而弩正是後者最趁手的武器。
tacticsEn: The whole rising was compressed into a few li between the inner palace city and the outer ward, and it lasted no more than a single day. Chen Shuling's plan was a court-style seizure of power: first he gathered his followers and his money while Emperor Xuan was still dying; then, after the emperor's death, he struck inside the Yunlong Gate with the poisoned knife, hoping to dispose of his brother in one blow, broke away back to the Eastern Office, used the authority of his office as Yangzhou Governor to call in armoured men, scattered wealth to buy them, and tried to make the princely generals abroad believe that the new ruler was already in his hands, so that he could concentrate his troops and break out through the South Gate to run for Sui. Xiao Mohe's reply had three stages. First, he accepted no offer made on terms of a ministry of three dukes; instead he set a counter-condition, that the prince's own trusted general must come in person, which tempted the rebels into handing over Dai Wen and Tan Qilin, whom he seized and beheaded and then displayed at the East City, breaking the morale of the rebel force before any clash. Second, he shut the palace gates and the roads running to the South Gate, with the guard waiting in the doorways with crossbows, so that the bolts covered the street mouths and the rebels could not deploy. Third, when Chen Shuling finally led a hundred men, horse and foot, in a dash for the South Gate, he concentrated his troops on the key roads and cut them down: the prince, in his haste to reach Sui, fell from his horse and was killed, and the hundred men with him scattered. In terms of troop types this was a typical close-range rebellion: the attackers relied on the sudden opening of a gate, on confused close fighting and on a breakout, while the defenders relied on the closing of gates, on blocking the roads and on shooting from fixed points. The crossbow was precisely the weapon that suited the second of these two methods.
data: 可核的數字不多，但都見於《陳書》與《資治通鑑》。時間：太建十四年正月甲寅，宣帝崩；翌日正月乙卯，始興王叔陵作逆，是日即伏誅，從發動到平定不過一日。兵力：叔陵在東府所集為甲士與自己的常備部曲，突圍時自率步騎百餘人，這支隊伍是叛軍全部的突擊力量；蕭摩訶一方是京師宿衛、殿中侍衛與追捕隊伍，另有尚書台調來的宮禁人馬。官秩與封邑：陳叔陵十六歲封始興郡王，開府都督江郢晉三州諸軍事，後歷湘州刺史、鎮南將軍、揚州刺史，至太建十一年復為侍中、中軍大將軍；他早年在梁為人質，歸陳後封康樂侯，邑五百戶。人物：被擒斬並懸於東城的有戴溫、譚騏驎二人；附逆被誅的宗室有新安王陳伯固；叔陵諸子被賜死，舅父彭暠與相關官員被處決。外部時序：開皇二年十月，隋文帝分道出師伐陳，兵鋒已抵江淮，距京師兵變約九個月，叔陵出奔隋朝正是要趕上這一波北方出兵。地理：叛亂起於皇城雲龍門，集合點為東府，示眾處為東城，終結點在南門外的通道上，全線都在建康城內數里之間。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are few, but those that exist are recorded in the Book of Chen and the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Government. On timing: on the jia-yin day of the first month of the fourteenth year of Taijian Emperor Xuan died; the next day, on the yi-mao day of that same first month, the Prince of Shixing Chen Shuling rebelled, and he was executed the same day, so the whole affair lasted no more than one day from outbreak to suppression. On troops: what Shuling gathered at the Eastern Office was armoured men and his own standing retainers, and when he broke out he led no more than a hundred men, horse and foot, which was the entire striking force of the rebels. On the other side Xiao Mohe had the capital garrison, the Palace Guard and his own pursuing force, reinforced by palace troops sent out by the Department of State Affairs. On rank and fief: Chen Shuling was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing at sixteen and given an independent command over the armies of Jiang, Ying and Jin; he later became Governor of Xiang, General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Yangzhou, and in the eleventh year of Taijian was once more made Attendant and General of the Central Army. He had earlier been a hostage in Liang, and after the family returned to Chen he was made Prince of Kangle with five hundred households of fief. On persons: two men, Dai Wen and Tan Qilin, were seized, beheaded and hung at the East City; the only member of the imperial clan who joined the plot, Chen Bogu, Prince of Xin'an, was executed; the prince's sons were given ordered deaths, and his uncle Peng Gao together with the officials involved were put to death. On external timing: in the tenth month of the second year of Kaihuang the Sui emperor sent several armies east against Chen, the spearhead already reaching the Yangtze and Huai, roughly nine months after the rising in the capital, and Shuling's flight to Sui was an attempt to catch that northern expedition in progress. On geography: the rising began at the Yunlong Gate of the inner palace, the mustering point was the Eastern Office, the place of public execution was the East City, and the end of the matter was on the road outside the South Gate; the whole affair was contained within a few li of Jiankang.
cause: 起因是皇位繼承的真空與宗室權力的過度集中。陳宣帝太建十四年正月病重京師，尚未安排身後事，宣帝一崩，長子陳叔寶與次子陳叔陵同時失去可以依循的裁定者；叔陵出繼祖父陳道譚，本無排行上的優勢，但他十六歲便出鎮江州、掌三州軍務，此後又做過湘州、揚州刺史與中軍大將軍，握有兵柄與部曲，形成了足以與皇位爭雄的私人力量。他性情嚴刻，屬下畏懼，歷任上州刺史時各州鎮聞其到達都震恐，說明他早已有調動武力的實力與便利。直接導火線是那把藥刀：宣帝崩後他趁侍疾刺傷兄長頸項，本望一擊得手，事敗被縛，才被迫把陰謀變成明面上的舉兵；而北周降將與北方來使在建康往來、同年十月隋軍已將大舉東下，更讓他判定陳朝守不住、自己必須另找出路。於是全部風險被押在一夜之間：在外諸王將帥無人響應、宿衛只聽尚書台調度、宮禁出入有人把守的建康城裡，靠一柄淬藥的刀和東府一群甲士去奪一個剛剛成立的朝廷。
causeEn: The cause lay in a vacuum in the succession and in the excessive concentration of power in the hands of the imperial clan. In the first month of the fourteenth year of Taijian Emperor Xuan lay dying in the capital without having settled what would follow his death, and when he died both Chen Shubao, the eldest son, and Chen Shuling, the second, lost the one man whose word had settled such questions. Shuling had been adopted to continue the line of his grandfather Chen Daotan and had no advantage in the order of succession, yet at sixteen he was sent out to govern Jiangzhou with command over three provinces, and afterwards held the posts of Governor of Xiang, Governor of Yangzhou and General of the Central Army, keeping troops and retainers of his own, so that he had built up a private military power strong enough to contest the throne. His manner was harsh and exacting and his subordinates were afraid of him; when he arrived as governor the prefectures and garrisons of the realm trembled, which shows that he had long had both the means and the convenience to move troops. The immediate trigger was the poisoned knife. After the emperor's death he struck at his brother's neck while the latter attended the sick bed, hoping for a single decisive blow; when that failed and he was bound, he was driven to turn a plot into open rebellion. The movement of former Northern Zhou officers and northern envoys through Jiankang, and the fact that the Sui army was about to march east in force in the tenth month of the same year, convinced him that the Chen could not hold and that he must find another way out. So he staked everything on a single night: inside a Jiankang where none of the princes and generals abroad answered his call, where the garrison obeyed only the Department of State Affairs and where the gates of the palace were watched, he meant to take a just-born court with one poisoned blade and the armoured men of the Eastern Office.
impact: 短期看，這場兵變替陳後主清掉了宗室內部最大的一股競爭力量，也讓他坐穩了尚書台的位置；但陳朝最缺的就是能打的兵與能用的將，陳叔陵留下的江南州鎮與部曲隨之被拆散、收歸朝廷，宗室在軍中的分量被削弱，這正是開皇二年十月隋軍東下時南朝最沒有還手能力的時候。技術上，這一役把蕭摩訶這位以步弩立身的將領推到了南陳權力核心，也讓陳朝的弩兵體系被更多人看見：它善守、能壓制、適合城防與近距封鎖，卻救不了宮廷裡的權力真空。蕭摩訶後來率部降隋，成為隋軍平陳的前線主將之一，開皇十九年隋軍南下建康時他已是隋方將領；換句話說，陳朝自己人用弩守住的那座城，最後還是被同一批熟識弩兵與江防的降將從內部打開。歷史上的回聲也延伸到隋唐：陳朝末年的宗室內鬥、宿衛失控與大將被俘後降北，成為隋滅陳過程中最典型的內部崩解樣本。
impactEn: In the short term the rising removed the largest single rival faction inside the imperial clan for Emperor Hou of Chen and confirmed his position at the head of the Department of State Affairs. But what the Chen state lacked above all was soldiers who would fight and generals who could be used, and the provincial commands and private retainers that Chen Shuling had built were broken up and folded back into the central government, reducing the weight of the imperial clan in the army. That was precisely the moment when Southern Chen had least power to answer, in the tenth month of the second year of Kaihuang, when the Sui armies came east. Technologically the affair pushed a man like Xiao Mohe, who had made his name with the handheld crossbow, to the centre of power in Southern Chen, and it made the crossbow system of the Chen more widely known: it is good at defence, it can pin an opponent down, it suits city defence and close-range blocking, and yet it cannot fill a vacuum of authority in the palace. Xiao Mohe later went over to Sui with his troops and became one of the leading Sui commanders in the conquest of Chen; when the Sui armies marched on Jiankang in the nineteenth year of Kaihuang he was already a general on the Sui side. In other words, the city that had been held by Chen's own men with their crossbows was finally opened from within by the same men, who knew the crossbow troops and the river defences all too well. The echo of the affair runs on into the Sui and Tang as well: the infighting of the imperial clan, the loss of control over the palace guard and the surrender to the north of generals who had been captured became the standard example of internal collapse in the process of Sui's conquest of Chen.
result: 結果是迅速而徹底的。始興王陳叔陵從雲龍門逃回東府、散金銀召甲士之後，蕭摩訶先以反條件誘出其心腹戴溫、譚騏驎，擒送臺省斬首並在東城示眾，斷其臂膀；叔陵見無援兵可恃，遂自率步騎百餘人由南門突圍，準備渡江投奔正在攻陳的隋朝，途中落馬，被蕭摩訶率軍追斬於城外通道之上。附逆的新安王陳伯固被誅，叔陵諸子賜死，其舅父彭暠與相關官員被處決，東府所聚兵眾解散，尚書台重新掌控宮禁與宿衛。自太建十四年正月乙卯起算，陳朝最大的一次宗室兵變在一日之內結束，陳後主得以繼續統治，而代陳的隋朝也從此不必再考慮江南宗室另立旗號的風險，直接把南進的時間表推到了開皇十八年至十九年。
resultEn: The outcome was quick and total. After Chen Shuling had fled from the Yunlong Gate back to the Eastern Office and scattered gold and silver to call in his men, Xiao Mohe first used a counter-condition to draw out his intimates Dai Wen and Tan Qilin, seized them, sent them to the Department of State Affairs to be beheaded and hung them at the East City, cutting off the prince's arm. Seeing that no help was coming, Shuling led a hundred men, horse and foot, in a dash through the South Gate, meaning to cross the river and throw himself on the Sui army that was then attacking Chen; he fell from his horse on the way and was cut down by Xiao Mohe's pursuing force on the road outside the city. Chen Bogu, Prince of Xin'an, who had joined the plot, was executed; the prince's sons were given ordered deaths; his uncle Peng Gao and the officials involved were put to death; the troops mustered at the Eastern Office were dispersed, and the Department of State Affairs took back control of the palace guard and the inner gates. Counting from the yi-mao day of the first month of the fourteenth year of Taijian, the largest rising by an imperial prince in the history of the Chen was over within a single day. Chen Shubao was able to go on ruling, and the Sui, which was to replace the Chen, no longer had to weigh the risk of the southern imperial clan raising a rival banner and could push its timetable for the southern advance forward to the eighteenth and nineteenth years of Kaihuang.
